The telemetry shows a textbook macro-based initial access: a Word document (invoice.docm) was opened via WINWORD.EXE, and exactly 60 seconds later Word spawned powershell.exe with a base64-encoded command that decodes to "IEX" (Invoke-Expression) — a classic macro-triggered PowerShell download-and-execute cradle (MITRE T1566.001 Spearphishing Attachment, T1204.2 User Execution, T1059.001 PowerShell, T1027 Obfuscated Command). Only one host has telemetry in this environment: AZ-EVAL-26667237. No other hosts, and no network, file, or registry data streams, were found for this incident (confirmed via index discovery), so lateral movement, C2 callback, and payload drop cannot be confirmed or ruled out — this is the primary data gap. The automated IoC-extraction tool's query failed against this environment's reduced schema (missing destination.ip, file.path, registry.*, hash, and executable fields), so the IoC set below was built manually and directly from the two process-start events per the forensic skill's fallback guidance; it is narrow but fully evidence-backed.

Full host isolation is not yet justified: there is no network or lateral-movement telemetry (positive or negative) to indicate spread beyond this single process, so the more proportionate response is to terminate the malicious process and its descendants rather than disrupt the entire host.
